title: Kitchen Drainage Maintenance: Preventing Grease Buildup in P-Traps
description: Educational guide explaining how grease solidifies inside kitchen sink P-traps and how routine maintenance prevents drain restrictions.
image_prompt: A clean, professional 9:16 vertical educational cutaway illustration of a residential kitchen sink drain assembly under an open cabinet. The image shows a realistic white PVC P-trap connected to a stainless steel sink drain assembly at the top and a wall drain pipe at the back. The lower bend of the P-trap is rendered in a clear cross-section, revealing the interior of the pipe. Inside the trap dip, a visible layer of yellowish grease residue is shown sticking to the lower interior pipe walls beneath standing water, while clear water attempts to pass through. The piping geometry is physically realistic with correct slip-nut fittings, wall escutcheon, and standard 1.5-inch tubular drainage proportions. Professional studio lighting under the cabinet, crisp focus, photorealistic textures for PVC and stainless steel. No text, no labels, no arrows, no watermarks, no logos, no fake branding.
visual_story: The visual uses a clear sectional view of an under-sink P-trap to show where kitchen waste settles. Viewers can see how liquid fats and cooking oils cool down when they hit the standing water trapped inside the P-trap bend. As the grease cools, it attaches to the PVC interior walls, gradually narrowing the drainage path. This visual directly links unseen pipe blockages to daily kitchen habits.

on_image_text.explanation: Warm fats and oils cool down upon entering standing trap water, adhering to interior pipe walls.
on_image_text.takeaway: Scrape fats into the trash and flush drains routinely with hot water and dish detergent.
